story: On a sunny Sunday morning in Sumter Oaks, Gary is checking his golf cart's battery and testing the roof frame before sketching out where the light strip and speakers will go. Over on Magnolia Loop, Donna is hauling extra flamingos behind a hedge so that only three are visible from the street, while Hal works through his violation notebook, updating the entries on Gary's cart mods and Donna's flock. Rosa, content as ever, is washing up from last night's dinner and setting out coffee things for Hal's porch visit, and the town is left with the morning-after mess of candy wrappers and a sagging inflatable ghost, plus a reminder from Town Hall that Halloween decorations must come down by November 7.
events: Town news: The morning after Halloween: candy wrappers on the sidewalks, a slumping inflatable ghost, and a note at Town Hall asking that Halloween decorations come down by November 7.

Donna (donna flamingo flock): Pull the extra flamingos behind the hedge, leaving just three visible from the street

Rosa (rosa kitchen): Wash up from last night's dinner and set out coffee things for Hal's porch visit

gary.thought_process: The parade's over and the morning is quiet. I'm home at the workbench with the cart right here, and my last note was to inspect the battery and roof frame and sketch where the light strips and speakers go. Gary-style, I should get my hands on the project. Law L-01 says exterior mods visible from the street need Architectural Review approval, so I'll keep the plan on paper for now and check the battery and frame first. Holiday lighting is allowed from Thanksgiving, so there's no rush to bolt anything on today. Working on it also keeps the house from feeling too quiet.

parameters.content: Check the battery charge and test the roof frame, then sketch the light strip and speaker layout

donna.thought_process: It's a bright Sunday morning on Magnolia Loop and I'm alone out here. The parade and costume contest are over, and I promised Hal I'd thin the flock to three flamingos so the street stays tidy. L-02 says no more than three ornaments can be visible from the street, so I should handle it right now before anyone complains. Gary and I had a great court session, but there's nobody around to talk to anyway. Time to move the extras behind the hedge.

parameters.content: Pull the extra flamingos behind the hedge, leaving just three visible from the street

hal.thought_process: Quiet Sunday morning, nobody in sight. My last notebook entry from Tick 297 was a plan to review the Gary and Donna entries, and it's still sitting there. Parade's over, so the carts are back on the street in plain view. I'll go through the notebook and update the counts before I take my binoculars out to Magnolia Loop. Facts first, then I decide whether anybody gets reported. Rosa's coffee is tomorrow, and I'd rather walk in with my records straight.

parameters.content: Review and update entries on Gary's cart modifications and Donna's flamingo count

rosa.thought_process: It's Sunday morning, nobody's around, and I'm home. Last tick I already checked my per-diem shifts, so I'm clear for Hal's coffee on the porch tomorrow. The dinner went well and all three neighbors came, which was my big goal. Now I should do something practical for tomorrow: get the kitchen ready, coffee supplies set, maybe tidy up after last night. I'll use the kitchen to clean up and get the porch coffee ready rather than wander off with nobody to talk to.

parameters.content: Wash up from last night's dinner and set out coffee things for Hal's porch visit

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
